html:
Hergé, the pen name of Georges Remi, was a Belgian cartoonist from Brussels who created the comic hero Tintin in 1929.

The Adventures of Tintin follow a young reporter and his dog Snowy around the world, from the Soviet Union to the Moon. The 24 albums have been translated into dozens of languages and sold hundreds of millions of copies. His clean drawing style, called the clear line, shaped European comics.

Early albums carry the colonial and racial prejudices of their time, especially Tintin in the Congo, about the Belgian Congo, which is still debated. Hergé worked for a newspaper controlled by the German occupiers in the Second World War, which damaged his reputation. Brussels remains a centre of the comic strip. See Belgium.
sum: Hergé, the pen name of Georges Remi, was a Belgian cartoonist from Brussels who created the comic hero Tintin in 1929.
